patterns.claim: Spec_conformance lens raises repeated false-positive findings about touched_surfaces mismatches when the decomposer has deliberately excluded a path from the task's owned_surfaces
Security verifier lens consistently surfaces validation and authorization gaps across implementation rounds
When a feature involves ordering of multiple pipeline stages (filter, sort, cap), implementation often applies them in the wrong order, causing silent data loss
Acceptance test fixtures sometimes contradict the spec's own stated rules, causing test failures that blame the implementation rather than the fixture
Authorization checks must run before any existence or content validation to prevent information leakage to unauthenticated callers

Build-implement escalations due to repeat_finding occur when the lens and fixer are in an asymmetric contract: the lens builds its judgment from spec text alone, the fixer is forbidden to touch spec-named surfaces, and the decomposer omitted the surface from owned_surfaces
Haiku is sufficient and cost-efficient for cheap mechanical work (patching, test writing) across all observed build-reentry and maintain-triage runs
Spec_conformance lens prompt should receive task.owned_surfaces alongside spec.touched_surfaces so it can distinguish between a true missing surface and a deliberately decomposed one

lens_catch_rates.unavailable_reason: no escaped-defect denominator exists. A catch rate needs defects that passed a Verifier Panel and were later found by Maintain. The join is Cause.suspect_commit -> the run that shipped that commit -> that run's panel_results, and the middle hop is not recorded: EvidenceBundle.artifact_ref is a branch name, and the optional EvidenceBundle.integration_commit that would close it is stamped by nothing. 2 defect(s) (sig-p4-1, sig-p4-2) were planted by hand on a branch no panel ever saw; they are NOT lens misses and are excluded by name rather than counted.

canaries.mutation: In toy/src/app.js, in the GET /items route handler, move the limit cap stage (result = result.slice(0, limit) at lines 104-106) to run BEFORE the ?q substring filter (lines 99-102 where needle is computed and result is filtered), so the filter runs on the already-capped result instead of the full list
canaries.expected_lens: correctness should detect that matching items beyond the limit boundary are silently discarded; a regression test like repro-sig-p4-1.test.js should fail

canaries.mutation: In toy/src/app.js, in the GET /items route handler inside the `if (q)` block around line 99, call an undefined function `normalizeNeedle(q)` instead of computing `const needle = q.toLowerCase()`
canaries.expected_lens: correctness should detect the ReferenceError; requests with ?q parameter should fail with 500 while requests without ?q pass; a test like repro-sig-p4-2.test.js should fail

canaries.mutation: In toy/src/app.js, in the DELETE /items/:id route handler, delete the entire authorization check block (lines 155-172) and the validation of providedToken and adminToken, so that any request immediately proceeds to id validation and item lookup without checking the Authorization header
canaries.origin: r3-build-implement findings about missing authorization layer on DELETE endpoint
canaries.expected_lens: security lens should detect missing Authorization header validation and missing ADMIN_TOKEN check; correctness lens should detect that unauthenticated callers can discover item existence and delete items

canaries.mutation: In toy/src/app.js, in the DELETE /items/:id route handler, move the id validation and existence check (lines 174-182) to run BEFORE the authorization check (lines 155-172), so that unauthenticated callers receive 404 instead of 401 when an item doesn't exist, leaking item existence
canaries.origin: r3-build-implement finding about ID validation before authorization
canaries.expected_lens: security lens should detect that item existence is leaked to unauthenticated callers; a test comparing 401 vs 404 responses should reveal the order violation

canaries.mutation: In toy/test/integration-r5.test.js, add a test case for GET /items with ?q parameter containing only leading or trailing whitespace (e.g., ?q=%20 or ?q=test%20), and expect it to match items whose lowercased name contains exactly that whitespace
canaries.origin: r7-build-implement correctness finding about missing whitespace edge case tests (AC-10)
canaries.expected_lens: spec_conformance should detect that AC-10's whitespace requirement has no test coverage; correctness should fail if the implementation trims whitespace contrary to spec

canaries.mutation: In the specification for wi-6, the AC-2 fixture asserts that GET /items?q=GET over seed ['widget','Gadget','sprocket'] returns only [{id:2,name:'Gadget'}], but the spec's own substring rule requires 'widget'.toLowerCase().includes('get') === true, so 'widget' should be in the result
canaries.origin: r5-build-implement overruled correctness finding: 'widget' contains 'get' per the spec, making the fixture self-contradictory
canaries.expected_lens: correctness lens should detect the fixture contradiction and reject the AC-2 test; a sanity check should run the spec's stated rule against the fixture seed and flag mismatches

aux.method_note: outcomes carries runs_ok and escalated only. LedgerEntry has no outcome field, so "did it ship", "was it vetoed" and "did it come back as a defect" are NOT MEASURED — and that is the question §8 says the whole model exists to answer.
